answer: Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. Each submission hangs on the forge of a task receipt, and the nadir is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. The saffron of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short.
